mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises above 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate coupled with rising rates indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates strong supply activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in CPI suggests inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If CPI increases by more than 0.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts and retail sales increase together, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both housing starts and retail sales increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment and high federal funds rate indicate impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4% and FEDFUNDS is above 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.
